active_family: one-shot support-valid transition flow capped; recurrent support-valid transition flow next
current_bottleneck: One-shot support-valid transition flow learns plausible support-safe transition noise but does not make the expected transition law sufficiently state-dependent. Feeding implied state into the one-shot velocity improves mean reversion, but only partially and with robustness regressions, so the bottleneck is native recurrent state dependence rather than another one-shot feature.
last_result_summary: 301a scored 4/11 and 302a scored 3/11. 302a improved MR ratio from 0.031 to 0.332 and MR h30 from 0.166 to 0.417 while preserving explosion 0.0%, but it still failed mean reversion and level KS, and it regressed cointegration worst-cell robustness plus q99 jump cells. The mechanism is clear enough to abandon more one-shot state-exposure tweaks.
next_step_recommendation: Run a paradigm shift to a recurrent support-valid transition generator: the model should sample one logit-IV transition at a time, update the generated state on support, then condition the next transition on the actual generated history/state. Keep the core vanilla and avoid low-rank, bounded paths, replay, or evaluator-specific losses.
